description: Grupo conformado por estudiantes de la institución educativa Futura Schools, sede Cerro Colorado.
summary:
Sol Zero is a 2D educational RPG created to introduce children to the real-life challenges, daily responsibilities, and psychological pressures faced by astronauts living in space and, in the case of the game, on Mars. Instead of presenting space exploration purely as action and adventure, the game puts players in charge of managing a Martian habitat dome and its daily operations, where every decision directly impacts the survival and well-being of the crew.

To address the challenge of making complex space science accessible and engaging for younger audiences, Sol Zero translates authentic aerospace concepts into intuitive gameplay mechanics. Players must balance critical resources, maintain the dome’s life-support environment, manage communication delays with Earth, and closely monitor crew mood and mental health during long-duration missions.

This project matters because future deep-space exploration depends not only on advanced engineering, but also on human resilience, teamwork, and early STEM inspiration. By letting kids experience what it truly takes to live and work off-Earth, Sol Zero sparks curiosity about science and space careers while teaching empathy, problem-solving, and strategic thinking in a fun, memorable way.
details:
What does it do?

Sol Zero is an educational 2D role-playing simulation designed to teach children about the realities of human spaceflight. Specifically:

  • It simulates the daily management and operational challenges of living inside a Martian habitat dome.
  • It monitors critical life-support resources and environmental conditions under pressure.
  • It introduces crew mood and mental health management during long-duration space missions.
  • It replicates communication delays and tasks between the Martian dome and Earth.
  • It centralizes these concepts into an interactive, kid-friendly experience to make aerospace science accessible.

How does it work?

The project follows an engaging gameplay loop:

  1. Habitat Management: Players take charge of the Martian dome interface to oversee daily survival routines.
  2. Resource & Crew Balancing: Players must maintain life-support systems while keeping a close eye on the crew's emotional well-being and stress levels.
  3. Operational Decision-Making: Players respond to simulated events, handle Earth communication tasks, and make strategic choices to ensure the mission's success.

What benefits does it have?

  • Educational: Translates complex aerospace science, life-support mechanics, and psychological challenges of space into intuitive, hands-on learning for children.
  • Social & Inspirational: Sparks early curiosity and passion for STEM fields, showing that space exploration relies as much on human teamwork and mental resilience as it does on technology.
  • Accessibility: Designed as a lightweight, browser-based game that runs smoothly without heavy hardware constraints.

What is the intended impact of the project?

In the short term, our goal is to provide an engaging, accessible educational tool that introduces children to the realities of human spaceflight and STEM concepts through interactive play. In the long term, we aim to inspire a new generation of students to pursue careers in science, engineering, and space exploration, demonstrating that future missions depend just as much on teamwork, adaptability, and mental health as they do on technology.

How is your project creative?

Sol Zero shifts away from traditional space combat or pure action tropes to focus on the human and psychological side of living off-Earth. Instead of treating space exploration solely as an engineering challenge, our game blends emotional management, communication delays, and resource strategy into a kid-friendly 2D RPG format, making abstract aerospace realities relatable and fun.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Age-Appropriate Pacing: Designing intuitive mechanics that keep young players engaged without overwhelming them with overly technical jargon.
  • Scientific & Psychological Realism: Accurately reflecting real-life astronaut challenges—such as isolation, delayed communications with Earth, and daily life-support maintenance—adapted to a Martian habitat dome scenario.
  • Visual & Interactive Clarity: Ensuring clear visual feedback so players immediately understand how their decisions impact both the dome's environment and the crew's mood.
  • Technical Accessibility: Building the game with HTML so it runs smoothly in any standard web browser without requiring heavy hardware or complex installations.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Development & Prototyping: General AI tools (used primarily as a brainstorming and organizational aid to structure concepts and workflow; minor support during code creation).
  • Programming Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript.
  • Frontend & Architecture: Lightweight browser-based web architecture ensuring smooth performance without local installations.
  • Hardware: Standard development and testing computers.
